scope: Assess reported HBB DNA reporter design using target sequence, directional-primer metadata and backbone records. Assay outcomes are not used to map the design or define sequence features; exact reporter RNA remains unestablished.

reported_design.supplement_table1: HBB MPRA uses pGL4.11c in HEL92.1.7; fragment187bp.
reported_design.supplement_table18: Directional amplification/cloning oligos support native-HBB-orientation insertion.
reported_design.backbone_MCS: Both deposited pGL4.11b and pGL4.11c have an altered MCS upstream of the annotated luc2 sequence.
reported_design.MCS_consistency: Forward flank and reverse flank order are consistent with the native-minus-oriented insert upstream of luciferase.
reported_design.barcode_location: Main text reports luciferase insertion between regulatory element and tag; tag becomes reporter3primeUTR.

conclusions.physical_DNA_insert_orientation: Reported design is consistent with native HBB minus-strand orientation, not the plus-strand coordinate target representation.
conclusions.reporter_RNA_5prime_end_or_native_TSS_us: Not established by these sources or by the barcode RNA/DNA readout.

limitations: The deposited records are cloning backbones, not an independently sequence-verified complete HBB library molecule.
Reported construct design and primer consistency do not establish every physical molecule or its transcription start.
Native-TSS initiation would predict transcription of native UTR sequence; alternative reporter initiation is not ruled out.
Barcode RNA abundance is not direct protein production, translation efficiency or hemoglobin physiology.
